title: Start the connectors that can start

blocks.text: The order service starts six integration connectors when it boots, and each connector's constructor opens its own connection. Last Tuesday the customs partner's API was down for an hour, and every restart in that hour failed: one connector that couldn't reach its partner kept the other five from starting. The week before, a connector with a plain bug in its constructor was skipped silently, and nobody noticed for two days.
`ConnectorFactory.createAll` already starts connectors and skips the ones that fail with a `ConnectorException`. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/ConnectorFactory.java`:

items: `create(type)`: a new connector made with the class's no-argument constructor.

blocks.text: When you're done, a connector whose constructor fails with a checked exception is skipped and the others still start, the `ConnectorException` carries the constructor's own exception as its cause, and an unchecked exception or an `Error` from a constructor reaches the caller exactly as it was thrown. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: every connector whose constructor succeeds is started, in order, and nothing is skipped
a class without a no-argument constructor is reported as a ConnectorException
a constructor that throws a checked exception makes create throw ConnectorException, so createAll skips that connector and starts the rest
the ConnectorException's cause is the exception the constructor threw, not the reflective wrapper around it
an unchecked exception or an Error from a constructor reaches the caller as it was thrown, not as a ConnectorException

origin.section: Class.newInstance Lets the Constructor's Checked Exception Escape Undeclared

concepts: Class.newInstance rethrows the constructor's exception as it is, so a checked exception escapes a catch of ReflectiveOperationException and the caller can't even catch it by type.
Constructor.newInstance wraps whatever the constructor throws in InvocationTargetException, whose cause is the constructor's own exception.
